**Diagnosis:** `incrObjectFieldByBulk` is absent from both [Mongo hash.js](/app/src/database/mongo/hash.js:214) and [Redis hash.js](/app/src/database/redis/hash.js:198). The existing methods increment one field at a time.

Mongo can use one upserted `$inc` document per key to update that key’s fields atomically. Redis needs a per-key server-side operation that validates existing fields before applying `HINCRBY`; its current batch is a pipeline, which cannot roll back earlier field increments.

The main uncertainty is partial success across keys: an unordered Mongo bulk or Redis pipeline can succeed for some keys and fail for others. Cache eviction must follow the keys that actually changed. Existing [hash tests](/app/test/database/hash.js:617) do not cover the new API.

I recorded the findings in `.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md`. No source or tests were changed because this run’s specialist instructions limit work to fault localization.

Implemented `incrObjectFieldByBulk` for [Mongo](/app/src/database/mongo/hash.js) and [Redis](/app/src/database/redis/hash.js). Shared validation checks tuple shape, safe integer increments, and field names before writing. Updates are atomic per key; successful keys have their cache entries invalidated.

Added coverage in [hash tests](/app/test/database/hash.js). The Redis hash suite passed (68 tests), ESLint passed, and `git diff --check` passed. Mongo integration tests could not run because `mongod` is unavailable.

VERDICT: FIX

**Code defect:** Mongo accepts a field named `bad.field` even though the requirements say to reject it. [increment.js](/app/src/database/increment.js:18) checks for dots after [hash.js](/app/src/database/mongo/hash.js:267) passes the name through `fieldToString`, which replaces the dot. A direct local call returned an update for `bad.field` instead of throwing. Validate the original field name before normalization.

**Tests:** `timeout 55s ./node_modules/.bin/mocha test/database.js --grep 'incrObjectFieldByBulk'` passed with 4 tests after I started a temporary Redis server. `timeout 55s ./node_modules/.bin/mocha test/database.js --grep 'Hash methods'` passed with 68 tests. I stopped the server afterward.

**TEST_ENVIRONMENT_PROBLEM:** The first targeted run failed in setup with `ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:6379`. Mongo tests could not run because `mongod` is unavailable locally. The Redis results do not cover the Mongo defect.
